methodology: MVP: Sleeper player search rank + actual league production (when available) + roster fit + starting-lineup impact.
headline: Payton Wins the Moore Deal on Fit and Form
verdict: Retirement Home is the current winner, with Payton holding the clearer edge in grade, fit, and lineup impact.
summary: Payton’s Retirement Home wins this transaction on the supplied evaluation: an 82.6 overall score, 88.5 roster-fit mark, and 76 lineup-impact score all beat Parker’s 78.4, 79, and 64. The central swing is DJ Moore, whose 70.7 value, No. 56 search rank, 9.9 season average, and 15.5 recent average give Payton the trade’s strongest current asset. Parker receives a useful RB in Woody Marks, but his recent average is below his season mark, while Elic Ayomanor’s recent production is only 1. Parker’s roster has six RBs and one TE, so the fit is understandable, but surrendering Moore leaves his side with the lower grade. Even the league’s resident trade lightning rod could not quite sell this one as a masterpiece.

sides.lore: Two-time champion (2020, 2021). Rivals: Parker, Andy, CJ, Alex.
sides.analysis: Payton sends Woody Marks and Elic Ayomanor but gets the trade’s most valuable piece in DJ Moore, plus Darren Waller for added TE depth. Moore carries a 70.7 value and No. 56 search rank, with a 15.5 recent average well above his 9.9 season average. Waller’s 4.9 recent average also edges his 4 season mark. Retirement Home has five RBs and two TEs, including Juwan Johnson, so this is not a desperation depth move; it is a quality-for-quality reshuffle that fits an 8-6 roster. The 88.5 fit score and 76 lineup-impact mark support Payton’s B- grade.
sides.bestReason: DJ Moore is the deal’s strongest asset, and his recent 15.5 average gives Payton the clearest production signal.
sides.biggestRisk: Payton gives up Woody Marks, whose 59.1 value and 9.5 season average make the RB-for-WR swap less comfortable if running-back depth becomes the priority.
